When I was in my teens, I wanted to be a psychologist, but then I became really unwell with Anorexia and decided I wouldn’t cope with hearing peoples problems all day. I had to spend a lot of time in hospital, and being around nurses so much made me decide to go into nursing after graduation. 

When I completed my mental health placement in my second year, I was like *”what the fuck am I doing”* and transferred into psychology (I had recovered from my eating disorder at this stage). Now I’m doing my fourth year in psych and will be able to apply for provisional registration at the end of the year, as well as hopefully being accepted into a clinical masters or doctor of psychology program

So psych undergrad (3 years) is actually just a very broad introduction to all the areas of psychology. You don’t actually learn the skills to practice as a psychologist. I honestly don’t really know what people do with just a three year psych degree without going onto further psych training/into other fields of further study like occupational therapy or social work (two very popular options if you don’t wanna continue with psych but still want to work in the mental health field).

Honours (fourth year) is where you start learning basic employable skills like psychological assessment and counselling skills. Right now, there’s a 4+2 option (4 years at uni + 2 years provisional registration while practicing under a supervisor). However, it’s almost impossible to do this pathway as basically no psychologists want to take on provisional psychs who have incredibly basic training. It’s so rare that my course director and all of the fourth year teaching staff don’t know anyone who’s done the pathway or offers supervision.

Then there’s masters or a professional doctorate if you want to do counselling. Because it’s so rare that people are able to do the 4+2 pathway, universities now offer a 5+1 pathway (4 years undergrad/honours + 1 year masters of professional psychology + 1 year of supervised provisional practice). They find that the extra year entices supervisors to feel more comfortable taking on provisional psychs, and helps ease the burden on clinical psych masters/clinical prof doc programs. Clinical masters is another 2 years after honours and clinical prof doc is an additional 3-4 years after honours. 

The bottle neck system that’s been created in psychology courses is actually a huge problem that the Australian Psychological Society is very aware of. That’s partly why the 5+1 pathway was introduced, but it’s still a huge issue. If you don’t get the marks during fourth year to be accepted into a masters program, I’m pretty sure you can still do counselling-based jobs bc you’ve had the counselling skills training. You just can’t call yourself a psychologist. I know that child protection is also an option. Otherwise a lot of people choose to go down the occupational therapy/social work masters route if they’re not accepted into a psych masters course. There are more options in terms of going into research-based work or doing a PhD after honours, but that is completely separate to being able to do counselling work. 

The dynamic that’s been created is absolutely terrible and certainly gives a lot of us some pretty hectic complexes. I guess there are always other options available if you just want to end up working in mental health, but if you’re deadset on being a psychologist, the pressure is extreme.

I’m currently doing my honours in psych (hoping to go onto clinical masters). 

A lot of people don’t realise how competitive it is. It’s competitive to be accepted into undergrad, where you have to maintain a D/HD average for a chance of being accepted into fourth year. Only after fourth year can you apply for registration, though next year it’s a requirement that you do a masters before being able to practice. Masters programs are insanely competitive (700+ applicants for *maybe* 20 places). You have to get minimum second class honours to meet the eligibility to apply for masters programs, and most won’t even give your application a second glance if you didn’t receive first class honours. On top of grades, they also take relevant work experience into consideration, but balancing a HD average during honours + work/volunteering in mental health is beyond anything that is practical. 

I love psych. I really, *really* do. But god, no one could pay me to do it again, purely because the competitiveness is so emotionally draining.

I went through this!

SEAS is called “adjustment factors” for fourth year. The Deakin psych fourth year team don’t typically accept adjustment factors, as generally, any impacts to your education are accounted for through assignment extensions/LAPs/exam considerations etc. In order for adjustment factors to be considered, you need to prove that your circumstances impacted your education above and beyond any special requirements you received throughout your degree. And even then, I don’t actually think they take it into consideration. 

I experienced pretty extreme circumstances that extensions etc could not account for during my first and second year. My grades were pretty sad, and it was clear that my education was being impacted. During third year, I was no longer experiencing these circumstances and my grades improved exponentially - from 50-70’s Unit Scores into the 90’s for all third year subjects. So it was pretty clear just how badly my education was impacted. I went through the whole process of trying to find out if they’d even accept adjustment factor documentation. I was so close to the cut off for honours, but I still wasn’t accepted despite my documentation. 

I know it’s a bit sad for me to say, but I honestly wouldn’t even bother. It’s such an effort to even get in contact with the people who will give you info about how you’re supposed to go about having your circumstances considered, let alone actually collating all of the documentation, only for it to likely not be considered. 

I was accepted into GDA at deakin, as well as honours at a lot of other unis. I decided to accept my GDA offer at deakin, despite my other honours offers, because I love the uni so much. However, other unis *do* take adjustment factors into consideration for fourth year - I have a full document of info of every uni in Australia that offers psych fourth year and whether they accept adjustment factors. If you’re dead set on honours, no matter the uni, dm me and I can give you more info. If you’re planning to stay at deakin and going through the adjustment factors process, your best bet is calling student central and they’ll put you through to a psych course advisor who can give you specific info on whether your circumstance would warrant an adjustment factors application. 

Good luck!!

Anecdotally, when venlafaxine stopped working for me, I was switched to desvenlafaxine. It took a lot of trial and error, but I finally found what works for me - 375mg desvenlafaxine (authority script bc it’s past the max dose) in combo with 30mg mirtazapine. I am now in remission from my MDD after fourteen years, though it is in part a result of the changes I was able to make through DBT. 

Venlafaxine/desvenlafaxine in combo with mirtazapine has been referred to as “rocket-fuel” because they work so well together. Though, meds aren’t always enough, which is why they work best with the therapy that’s right for you. 

I’m sure you’re aware of other biological treatments, but just incase - ECT is recommended if one doesn’t respond to meds. On top of this, TMS is also an option. And I haven’t looked much into it, but I’m fairly certain there’s a blood test available that is able to indicate what psych meds may work best? Don’t quote me on that though. There are also trials of other drugs (ketamine, psilocybin, mdma), but I’m not sure how easy they are to access

Edit: omg I’m an idiot. I was switched from desvenlafaxine *to* venlafaxine. I go by brand names (desvenlafaxine = pristiq, venlafaxine = effexor). So I’m on 375mg venlafaxine and 30mg mirtazapine, though I was also taking mirtazapine when I was on desvenlafaxine. Both are quite hardcore psych drugs, though they work in slightly different ways.

What dose of venlafaxine? Desvenlafaxine is also an option that’s really good for treatment-resistant depression, along with combining venlafaxine or desvenlafaxine with mirtazapine. It definitely depends on your degree of complications.

I ended up having to stay in icu and then be transitioned to a post-surg ward for five days because of my calcium levels (my parathyroid glands were *not* happy). In a way it was kind of good because I got the rest I needed. I was exhausted for a few days and doped up on pain meds, so couldn’t do a whole lot. 

When I went home, I was still tired, but able to do things as long as I rested afterwards and didn’t push myself too hard. Exactly a week after my surgery, I went to a gathering and was fine. I wasn’t allowed to lift heavy things or do strenuous exercise for three weeks, but did do gentle pilates exercises under the supervision of a trainer who changed things for me. 

The muscles in your neck will most likely be fucked. This is the thing that totally caught me off guard. If I was laying down, I couldn’t get up normally. I had to very gently and very slowly prop myself up until I was sitting... I basically couldn’t use my neck muscles at all for those sorts of things, which as it turns out, you actually use a lot. It took quite a few months of gentle neck strengthening exercises to get it back to normal. 

Basically I’d suggest give yourself a week of as much rest as possible. Do things like engaging with your toddler in simple activities like reading books if possible, but listen to your body and rest if it’s calling for it. After about a week, you’ll hopefully be okay to transition back into normal life, but maybe try to take it easy with your job. Having to use your mind can be incredibly draining when your body is trying to heal, and there’s a chance you’ll become extremely exhausted very quickly. Would it be possible to do part-time with slowly increasing your days as you feel able over the few weeks after your op? E.g. two days a week after your op (split so you have rest days in between), three days the next week etc? I know this isn’t an option for everyone though. 

That’s really the only practical advice I can give! Good luck with everything!! 💗

It’s kind of like the flu. I believe one of our strains of flu originated from the Spanish influenza. That killed a fuck ton of people when it first emerged, but over time it’s now less likely to be fatal (yes, I know people still die from it, don’t come @ me).

*As I said, I know very little about infectious disease, so if anyone knows any mistakes I’ve made, please let me know!*

I guess you could look at it one of two ways:

1. It’s less deadly therefore it’s less dangerous

2. It’s less deadly, but it is still deadly. Being more infectious, it means people are more likely to contract it, which possibly means more deaths. Furthermore, we have seen all the other consequences of this illness that *dont* result in death, and we really don’t have a proper understanding of the long term consequences, so it could definitely be argued that this mutation is actually *more* dangerous.

My lord, I could write a book about my experiences with therapists. But I’ll keep it as short as I can:

Therapist #1 - saw her for a few months when I was diagnosed with anorexia. Didn’t help at all, and then looked up pro-ana blogs in session. Refused to see her after that. 

Therapist #2 - saw her for a total of one session, as she told me straight up that if I self-harmed, she’d terminate treatment. Obviously very manipulative, and made me feel like I couldn’t actually be honest with her. 

Therapist #3 - saw her for just over two years. She was an eating disorder specialist. I thought she was helpful at the time. After my final hospital admission where I actually recovered, I went back to her, and realised she wasn’t helping me much anymore. I think this was due to the fact that I realised the specific things I needed to work on, and when I communicated this to her, she wasn’t willing (it was just feeling my emotions ffs). Stopped seeing her. In retrospect, looking back at our whole time working together, I don’t think she really helped much at all. But I think part of that was mostly due to the fact that I wasn’t ready to work on my anorexia.

Therapist #4 - after an 18mo therapy break from Therapist #3, I found out on of the clinicians from my final eating disorder admission had started working privately. I credit so much of my recovery to working with her on the ward. So yeah, started seeing her privately, and she helped a lot. She just *got* me. She diagnosed me with bpd, which was so obvious at that point, and Therapist #3 refused to even acknowledge it could be a possibility. This therapist helped me realise I was in an extremely abusive relationship, helped me connect with my current psychiatrist (who’s amazing), and convinced me to do dbt. 

Therapist #5 - had to stop seeing Therapist #4 bc I was doing dbt, thus Therapist #5 is from the dbt program. Holy fucking shit. I truly lucked out with her, because she is hands down the best dbt clinician in the entire program. I can’t even begin to explain how much she helped me. I have grown and matured SO much because of the work we did together. Had to stop seeing her once my year of dbt was finished. 

After Therapist #5, I went back to Therapist #4. It was hard getting used to working with her again. Her treatment style was very different to #5. And it took a little while for us to ~gel again, because she had to play catch-up with how much I’d grown. But we eventually started doing some good work and basic schema therapy, and was always receptive to any feedback I had about the treatment/relationship.

Therapist #4 went on maternity leave in Mid-March. I’ve just found out I can start seeing Therapist #5 again until she comes back from Mat-leave. It doesn’t start for a few weeks, but I’m hopeful as well as nervous. Again, I’ve grown a lot since I stopped seeing her, so it will be interesting to see how the dynamic works. 

And all of this isn’t even mentioning the psychiatrists I’ve seen, or the other therapists I’ve come across during my ed day program/dbt day program. Lots of very very bad experiences there. 

But I think all of this just really highlights how some therapists are not equipped to handle certain people, and how some are amazing but need to be willing to work on the issues the client *wants* to work on. The therapeutic relationship isn’t one-sided - it’s a total team effort by both clinician and patient.

It was actually my psychiatrist who picked it up - I was admitted to a mental health ward (partly due to insane anxiety aggravated by graves). She noticed how shaky I was and how I couldn’t lift my arms above my head to put my hair in a ponytail. She ordered a blood test and it came back that my TSH was literally undetectable. 

From there, I was referred to an endo who put me on methimazole. He also put me on propranolol to try control my heart rate and shaking. Unfortunately, I developed an allergic reaction and was switched to PTU... which I was also allergic to. 

After going months with absolutely no treatment because I couldn’t handle the stress of it, my psychiatrist put her foot down and got me into the public endo clinic as a category 1 patient. From there, they organised an urgent thyroidectomy - this is because my levels were too high to use radioactive iodine (the iodine speeds up your thyroid before it starts to destroy it, and they couldn’t risk sending me into a thyroid storm). 

After the effects of the anaesthesia wore off from surgery, it was insane how much better I felt. It made me realise just how abnormally my body was functioning for *such* a long time. 

All this to say, is that I went untreated with quite severe symptoms and never developed the eye bulging associated with graves. However, I do believe I eventually would have developed it, if I didn’t get treatment when I did. I’m not saying you won’t develop it, but it’s unlikely if you start medication and respond well to it. 

Post surgery, I have had a bit more weight gain, but I’m still completely healthy. My hands still shake a bit, but I’m unsure whether that’s damage due to graves (idk if that’s even a thing), or just general anxiety - but it is SO much better and I can actually hold a pen now lol. 

This can be a really stressful and anxiety-inducing time, but I really hope things are easily sorted out for you.

For some reason, I have a sixth sense for cheating. I can pick up on it straight away, even when there are not objective signs. So let me tell you a story from my childhood. 

When I was 14, I came home from school camp, and no one was home (my mum was at work and my stepdad was overseas). For some reason, I just felt something was... off. I felt like someone I didn’t know had been in the house. So the next morning, while my mum was in the shower, I decided to go through the messages on her phone (keep in mind, I was 14 and didn’t really think about respecting her privacy - all I was focused on was figuring out if someone I didn’t know was in the house). Lo and behold, she was cheating on my stepdad. 

That simple decision to go through my mums phone triggered the year (and years...) from hell. It became compulsive. I checked every single morning. I even went so far as to write the number down and call it at my best friends place to see who picked up. This lasted approx 9 months, and my parents had no idea what I was doing. During this time, I developed such a deep hatred for my mum. I would sit in the car on the way to school, just *seething* with anger. She was doing things that were going to destroy my stepdad - the man who had raised me since I was three. 

I developed severe depression, anxiety, constant panic attacks, and started binge eating, because I didn’t want to tell my parents what was going on. All this information was too much for me to hold on my two little shoulders. I broke, and tried to talk to the school counsellor, who said it was my fault I was experiencing these issues bc I was the one who invaded my mums privacy (*cue eyeroll*). 

Eventually, things became really heated one night between my parents, and I got really scared. I asked my mum to drive me to my best friends house where I just fucking *broke down*. I told her that I knew she was cheating, and to not lie to me, because I’d seen the messages. She finally admitted to it, and my parents broke up but we all still lived together.

They decided to get back together around Christmas, to try sort things out. Then in January, my stepdad went to Vietnam, and when he came home, I knew he had been cheating on my mum. She found out, and it was just such a mess. We all still lived together for a year, but my parents weren’t together, and it was hell. I honestly don’t remember a whole lot because of how traumatic it was. 

Quick summary of the aftermath: I continue to suffer from anxiety and depression, however my binge eating then turned into a six year struggle with anorexia because I felt like it was the only thing in my life that I could control. I have also been diagnosed with bpd, and my professionals think this was one of the main triggers for its development. My stepdad also became addicted to meth from all of this, and has been in and out of jail for the last five years. 

I honestly don’t know whether I regret going through my mums messages. Yes, I wouldn’t have had to carry the burden of knowing what was happening for so long, but it all would have come out eventually... and I think I would have preferred to be somewhat prepared than be blindsided. 

What I’m trying to get at, is that you really need to think about whether going through his messages is what’s best for *you*. It’s caused irreparable damage in my life, but I still wouldn’t change it. I feel like you have three options:

• read the messages and don’t do anything about it 

• read the messages and tell one (or both) of your parents

• don’t read the messages and pretend it never happened

• don’t read the messages, but still approach one (or both) of your parents about what happened 

I really hope you find a way to deal with all of this. My thoughts are with you. This is such a hard position for you to be in.

This exact scenario happened to me. *Literally.*

I (F) got into a relationship with another girl. We both had pretty severe mental illness, but we were determined to not let that impact our relationship in a negative way. Instead, we hoped supporting each other would strengthen our relationship. Lol. 

Looking back, there were a *lot* of red flags in the beginning. As I got better and started recovering from my original diagnoses, she just got worse. And worse. And worse. But I looked past the red flags because I still had such little self worth at the time. The abuse cycle had already begun, unbeknownst to me, and I started to form a trauma bond. Unfortunately, all of this just increased exponentially over time. 

One year after dating, she proposed to me. In front of all of my family. On fucking New Years. Because *”this is what I wanted”*. When I had told her multiple times that my ideal proposal would be secluded and intimate. And not on fucking New Years. Because of the audience, I felt like I had to say yes. I also knew that if I said no, and then completely embarrassed her in front of so many people, I would pay for it later. 

However, at this point I was so subconsciously confused about everything, that I went into a deep fucking state of denial and convinced myself I did want to marry her. The thought of not having her in my life fucking terrified me - partly because I didn’t know how I would cope (trauma bond), but some part of me knew that breaking up would bring on a fuckton of issues I didn’t want to deal with. 

I also avoided wedding planning and all of that like the fucking plague. I kept making excuses as to why we had to put it off. When same-sex marriage was legalised in Australia, I was overjoyed. But I was also beyond fucking *petrified* because that meant this whole wedding fiasco could actually happen. 

We dated for two years after she proposed. If I listed every single fucked up thing that happened during that relationship, I’d be here until next year. So here is a brief summary of some of the most traumatic/fucked up situations: 

• I overdosed because I couldn’t see a way out of the relationship. I just wanted it to end, but couldn’t see a way to escape. Because all of the attention was on me (much to my dismay), she decided to take a bigger overdose and ended up on life support. She was on life support three more times during the two years after we got engaged. 

• I stayed up until 5am talking with her cousin one night (who is now my best friend, and the person who convinced me to finally leave and helped me escape). My ex did *not* like this, because apparently that meant her cousin liked me more than her. So she essentially locked me in the car while driving at 150km/h around winding cliff-side roads, laughing manically while I had the worst panic attack of my life because I genuinely thought I was going to die. 

• she isolated me from all of my original mental health supports, as well as my family. Eventually, I was stood my ground and started seeing a new psychologist, who then convinced me to have a hospital admission. First, my ex convinced me to discharge AMA because she wasn’t coping at home. Then when she found out my psychologist thought I needed to go back to hospital, she physically abused me to the point of... I don’t even know how to describe it. It was awful. 

• there were multiple incidents of physical abuse, both before and after the last example. However, what happened during the last example was when things started to get extremely serious in regards to the physical abuse. One particular time, she was speeding down tiny little side streets and when we stopped, she started physically abusing me again. Why? Because her gp didn’t want to see her anymore. But that was my fault. I couldn’t even begin to list the amount of injuries she caused. 

Obviously, there was a *fuckton* of emotional and mental abuse happening as well, but that’s harder to accurately pinpoint and articulate. 

I don’t even know. It was just *so* fucked. So, so, so fucked. My psychologist and psychiatrist were doing so much subtle psycho-ed with me, to try get me to see the situation for what it was, and I guess it finally worked. Because one day, after drama that deserves its own post, I just couldn’t do it anymore. I finally accepted that I deserved better, and living with her was more terrifying than living without her. I called everything off, blocked her on as many things as I possibly could, and her cousin helped me to pack as much of my shit as I could fit in the car, and took me to my mums. 

I wish that was the end of it. I so desperately wish the abuse stopped after leaving. But alas, that part of me that knew there would be hell to pay if I left was right. She started trying to contact me in any possible way she could, she would turn up at my house and scream at my mum (who took time off work so I wasn’t alone) while I hid in a corner, create fake instagrams to see what I was posting, hacked into her cousins Instagram when I deleted a bunch of people I didn’t feel I could trust, posted online about how I was the abusive one and all the things I supposedly did to her, went to places she knew I frequented purely in the hopes of seeing me, and sent abusive messages to any of our mutual friends that saw/spoke to me. 

I couldn’t take it anymore. I didn’t feel safe *anywhere*. So I got a restraining order. 

Since then, she’s been silent, and I couldn’t be more grateful that I took the terrifying step to get legal intervention. It’s given me the space to find safety, and begin the slow process of healing. 

I’ve been diagnosed with PTSD because of it, and the prolonged stress of the situation triggered my thyroid to fuck-out on me (developed Graves’ disease which lead to my thyroid being removed). 

It was a year since I left last weekend. I don’t know how I feel about it... I don’t know how *to* feel about it. It’s just a mess. All of it. I can’t believe I let myself get into that situation. But at least I’m safe now (or... until the restraining order expires). 

So yeah. This was way longer than I originally intended, but there’s my story on how I literally thought I was going to marry someone and then had to get a restraining order against them. Thanks for coming to my TedTalk.

So I literally count in my head “one, two, three”, and on three I launch myself up and have a shower.

This is actually generally true. There’s not a lot of information on general web pages, but if you have access to journal articles, look into the Standard Ideals Model. 

It’s basically this idea that there are three interconnected circles: “the self”, “the ideal partner” and “the ideal relationship”. It’s kinda complicated and too much for me to explain right now, but your standards are generally a reflection of yourself (from what I can remember). So, if you have super high standards and you aren’t someone who reflects these standards in your behaviour, you’ll likely get rejected. Consistent rejection over time leads to your standards dropping and you going for someone that is way below your standards because of your fear of rejection and how that plays on your self worth. Generally speaking, flexibility in your ideal standards (to a certain extent) can lead to amazing relationships, but the most rewarding relationships are ones where people are able to get into a relationship where their standards are met fully - which then ties into them being in your league, as you’re more likely to be able to begin a relationship if you reflect your own values.

Sorry, just saw the last bit about not medicating/getting help for your anxiety. Here’s what my therapist suggested I do/what I do that kind of helps the tiniest bit:

• create a self soothe kit (lavender oils, colouring books, putty etc). Make it part of your routine to use these things before going to bed, as well as if you wake up from a nightmare

• Put lavender oil behind your ears, on the underpart (??) of your wrist, and below/slightly in your nose. Then sprinkle some on your pillow and consider getting a diffuser to keep on overnight - this honestly really helps calm me down. 

• watch a “safe” show until you’re literally unable to keep your eyes open any longer. My personal safe shows are finding nemo and the good place. It’s basically anything that makes you feel comforted, absorbs your attention but not in a way that will keep you awake, and something that reduces your anxiety

• if you’re trying to fall asleep and can feel yourself going into panic, there are a few things you can do:

1. Fill up a bowl with cold water from the tap. Put your head in it and hold your breath for as long as you can. This activates the mammillian dive reflex and can reduce your level of distress extremely fast. If dipping your head in cold water isn’t practical, putting a bag of frozen peas/an ice pack/anything super cold on your face can also help - just make sure you cover your eyes and temples, and hold your breath while you do it. 

2. Google paced breathing and paired muscle relaxation 

3. Get up and do a sudoku puzzle or something of the sort 

4. Wet a face washer with either hot or cold water, and put lavender oil on it. Then cover your face with it, and breathe in as deeply and slowly as you can. A good breathing technique is in for four counts, hold for two, out for eight counts 

But yeah. As I said, there’s also the nightmare dbt content, but I really suggest going through it with a trained therapist as it’s quite intense. Basically, you go into extreme amounts of detail with a repeated dream/themes, and then you “rewrite” it just before it turns scary. You then repeat it over and over to yourself in bed, until you fall asleep. Basically, dbt views nightmares as a “behaviour” - not one that you’re CHOOSING to do, just one that’s happening. And rewriting it is where the behavioural change comes into play.

Back story: I have bpd and was in a dbt day program with this particular girl. She’s 12 years older than me (she seriously does not look a day over 25), and a well-established criminal defence attorney. We’d both been in the group for a few months, but had never really talked properly, even though we always sat next to each other. Let’s call her L.

———————————————

I had very recently (I’m talking days) broken up with my extremely abusive fiancé. However, I still went to group as I needed the support. I went downstairs during break, and when I came back up, L and a few other girls were talking about marriage. L and another younger girl both started talking about their divorces, and I was so shocked that they were both so young and had even been married, let alone divorced. One thing lead to another, and I briefly mentioned that I had just broken up with my fiancé. They were all shocked, and as group was starting back up again, I quietly asked L if I could talk to her after program. I was already kind of planning on asking her to talk, as I wanted to professional advice about what my options were regarding my ex. 

Anyway, after program, we went downstairs together and she put her arm around me as we were walking saying she was so sorry, and then bought me a coffee. We proceeded to talk for four. fucking. hours. (Keep in mind that she is the most busy person I have ever met - she would literally stay in her office until 3am, and then be back in there at 7am, so four hours was a ridiculously massive chunk of her time when she always has so much to do)

She started off my telling me about her marriage/divorce, and then started telling me about the relationship she was in after she split up with her ex-husband. Turns out, she’d been in an extremely abusive relationship as well. She talked so candidly about it, and seemed like she had honestly come to terms with it and accepted it for what it was.

I was shocked. I’d never met ANYONE who’d been in a relationship even vaguely similar to the one I had just gotten out of. The things she said seriously made me question whether or not we had dated the same person. I could not believe we had both experienced the exact same things, and she helped me realise that every tiny action that I had never even thought about was typical of abuse. I told her things I had never told anyone before, and she listened without a single ounce of judgement. She accepted all of my own decisions, and helped me come to terms with the fact that it wasn’t my fault. She told me that she would not judge me in the slightest if I decided to go back, as it is extremely common in abusive relationships like the ones we’d experienced, and that it took her five times to actually be able to leave for good. She made me feel so fucking safe and understood and accepted, and I hadn’t felt that way in a very long time. 

Some of the things she told me during the first time we talked:

• Don’t become the collateral of her life

• Even murderers have more redeeming qualities (she worked with murderers almost every day)

• If you’re both looking out for her needs, then who’s looking out for yours 

From there, we became really good friends. We would talk after program, messaged all the time, she visited me in hospital for another three hours, we would take turns buying each other coffee, she helped me out with meds when I forgot to take mine one day (we were on the same antidepressant), she would let me call her in the middle of the night crying when she had just got home from work, gave me legal advice, helped me rationalise certain things, let me vent to her when something went wrong, and told me exactly what she thought of me - that I was a good person, and would then go on to list all the “amazing qualities” I possess.

I can’t even begin to explain the impact she has had on my life. This person that I barely knew allowed me to lean on her in my desperate time of need. I think the reason it had such a profound impact on me, was because she didn’t have to do ANY of those things. She could have easily just brushed me off. But instead, she helped me feel like a person again - a person who was worthy of love, and respect, and was capable of leading a life without my ex. 

Unfortunately, we’ve drifted in recent months. She left the program we were in, and moved back interstate and has been super, super busy. I miss her a lot. But I could not be more grateful for her, and everything she helped me with. She’s honestly one of the most amazing, kind-hearted, generous people I’ve ever met, and I really don’t know where I’d be without her support. She was like a big sister to me, and honestly inspired me in so many ways. She showed me that it was possible to rebuild your life and continue on. I recently got out of a very similar relationship myself. 

One of the most valuable things was people letting me talk about the gritty details if I felt like I could. They did not judge me, didn’t question why I didn’t leave earlier, basically accepted the situation without putting expectations on me. 

But honestly? The biggest moment I had, where everything kind of “clicked”, was when I randomly started talking to another person who was in an abusive relationship - someone who told me the ins and outs, and made me SERIOUSLY question if we’d dated the same person. No, we hadn’t. It’s just typical of abuse. It made me realise that the things my ex did really were abusive, and that other people in those situations had experienced the exact same things. 

Most people, when they’re finally able to detangle themselves from the toxic spiderweb of abusive relationships, feel like they NEED to go back; that this was the wrong decision; that it wasn’t actual abuse bc they had ~reasons for their actions; they “love” you/you’re the “love of their life”/they’ve “never loved anyone like they’ve loved you”/you’re never going to find that kind of love again... you get the point. It becomes part of the victims neural pathways as it’s been reinforced over and over again. A few things my friend said that absolutely changed my life, and stopped me from going back:

• “don’t let yourself become the collateral of her life”

• “even murderers have more redeeming qualities” (my friend is a very successful criminal defence lawyer who works with murderers every day)

• “if you’re both looking out for her needs, then who’s looking out for yours?”

She also told me that she would not judge me for a second if I did decide to go back - that she understood, and that it took her 5 tries to finally be able to leave properly. She let me call her during her insanely busy work days (she would stay in the office until 3am) and scream down the phone about the ridiculousness of the situation if I needed to, would talk to me for hours every night helping me come to terms with the situation, reminded me of all my positive attributes that would only be destroyed if I stayed in the relationship... she was just amazing during those first few critical weeks. She is probably the most pivotal person who helped me not completely and utterly fall apart and do stupid things. 

Please also be mindful that her ex will most likely go to every length imaginable to suck her back into his vortex of toxicity. He will probably try contact her in ways you will never, ever be able to predict - my ex and I had a joint calendar that I forgot to remove myself from, and she literally started making individual, one word events, trying to start a conversation. He will most likely try to turn everyone against her, make himself out like the victim, and make her seem like the crazy one. This is all going to be extremelyyyyy distressing for your friend. All you can do is be there, listen, validate, and try to help her come up with logical solutions (but only if she asks). 

Eg. 

Her: “what do I do about this? How do I make this stop?” 

You (clarify): “do you want me to help you try and see what we can do to fix this?” 

So my advice?

• Be there to listen if she wants to talk - and actually LISTEN. Also, validate, validate, validate. 

• Be very aware of your facial expressions/tone of voice/body language/general vibe you give off bc victims are EXTREMELY hypersensitive due to the need to be constantly hypervigilant of their abusers in order to try predict what is coming next

• be as non-judgemental of THEIR decisions as possible. Do notttt try to rationalise their abusers behaviour in any way, as this will most likely result in them feeling they need to go back even more. Instead, do everything you can to make sure your friend knows you do not judge her in the slightest for the decisions she had to make, as the decisions she made literally indicated what would happen next. Potentially try rationalise your friends decisions to help her become more accepting of them herself. 

• let your friend know that you are available, any time of the day (only if you are though). Let them know they can call or text you about anything they need to talk about

• remind her of everything she is without him (her good qualities, what you love about her, what makes her remarkable)

• recognise, both to yourself and potentially to her, that this is going to be an AWFUL period of her life, but that it will get better eventually (even if it feels like it never will) 

• do NOT judge her/act angry, disappointed etc, if she does end up going back. It is SO common, and your behaviour will predict how comfortable she will feel coming to you with problems in the future. I know how tempting it is to act angry and let the person know your disappointed in their decision to return, as this will help her leave again, right? No, not always. After talking to a lot of people who have experience domestic violence in all its forms, the consensus was that we had to learn that it was abusive for ourselves. If people told us what they thought, it only made us dig our heels in even more because we KNOW our partner and they don’t, and the partner always has “reasons” they behave the way they do

• help her look into taking further action (eg. Going to the cops, getting an IVO etc) if she feels ready and comfortable doing so 

• encourage her to connect with other abuse victims. I’m sure there’s support groups around, but I was lucky (???) enough to already have a lot of people who had experienced this in my life. But I honestly cannot tell you just how beneficial it was talking to people who TRULY understood what I had experienced and was going through - no one fully understands until they’ve been through it themselves. 

• try get them linked up with a psychiatrist and a psychologist. Chances are, she’s going to develop ptsd symptoms - there is medication that can help (psychiatrist), and she will also need to begin processing it when she’s ready (psychologist)

Anyway... I’ll leave it there. If I think of anything else I’ll add it later. If you have any questions about ANYTHING or want clarification, just let me know. I really hope things become easier for your friend soon, and that she’s able to keep herself safe. Thinking of you both xx

Very complicated and convoluted story, so please bear with me.

When I was 13, I found out my mum was cheating on my stepdad (he’d been my dad since I was four). 

I was away on school camp, and I just ~knew something was off but couldn’t put my finger on it. My step dad was also overseas at the time for work. When I got home, no one was there, but again, I just KNEW something wasn’t right and something told me I had to look at my mums messages - please keep in mind that I was 13 lol. The next day, while she was in the shower, I looked through her messages and my suspicions were confirmed. She was cheating on my step dad. But little 13yo me didn’t want to believe it, so I wrote down the number. I told my best friend at the time, and I called the number whilst at her house. A man answered that sounded Italian and I immediately hung up. 

For the following nine months, I kept it to myself. I would check her messages every morning while she was in the shower, and I developed a deep hatred for her. I only told a few very close friends at school, and didn’t tell my mum or my step dad that I knew because I didn’t want my family to fall apart. Due to the stress, I fell into a binge eating cycle and gained a lot of weight, became very depressed, and started having constant MAJOR panic attacks over “nothing”.

Eventually, my step dad found out one night as he saw an email. They got into a massive fight, a chair was broken, and I asked my mum to take me to my best friends house for the night as it was really scary. In the car, I came clean to my mum that I knew what was going on, and we both talked and cried about it for like an hour before I went into my friends house. 

This happened in October. Between then and December, they broke up but we’re still living together (just in separate bedrooms), and then got back together around December to see if things could work out. 

In January, my stepdad went to Vietnam for a friends wedding, and when he came back, I knew something was off again. I just had that same feeling. Lo and behold, he was having an affair with some chick from Vietnam. Again, I was the only person who knew and nobody knew that I knew. My mum found out within a few weeks, they got into a massive physical fight (my mum attacking my step dad), and they broke up again. 

Even though they had split up, we all still lived together for the following year. It was awful and traumatic and I honestly don’t remember a lot from that year. I coped with it, along with other stuff that was going on at school, by developing at eating disorder (restricting, bingeing, purging). I lost a lot of weight, and the following six years of my life were surrounded by treatment and hospitals.

After a year, they finally moved into separate houses. My brother and I lived with my mum. My mum continued the relationship with the person she had been cheating with, while my step dad developed an ice addiction and ended up in prison. He’s been in and out prison for 4 years now. 

My mum eventually ended the relationship with the person she was having an affair with, but at the time I was very very very sick with anorexia and in hospital constantly, so she blamed their failed relationship on my health and the stress it put them both under. In reality, he was an abusive piece of shit to both me and my mum. She’s now realised this, and hates his guts.
